mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen monotonically from -14.6 to -13.0 across the four weekly means, and each incremental return of commuters adds weekday foot traffic near offices, so RETAIL_REC keeps drifting upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -14.6 to -13.0 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: Next-28-day mean RETAIL_REC is at or below the last-28-day mean of -14.0 while WORKPLACES continues its four-week upward drift.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen every week from +6.7 to +5.9, indicating households progressively leaving home; that time reallocation converts into shopping trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 6.7 to 5.9 over the four weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed -14.0 in the two weeks following a further weekly RESIDENTIAL decline below +5.9.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT jumped from -39.3 to -37.4 in the final week, the largest single-week move in the snapshot; transit recovery precedes discretionary trip-taking, so RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks once transit holds above -38.

evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 1.9 points in the final weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays at or below its last-28-day mean of -14.0 for two weeks after TRANSIT holds above -38.0.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS stays below -35 while RESIDENTIAL falls, so outdoor alternatives remain suppressed even as households leave home; the freed time is captured by indoor commercial venues, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean below -35.0 and RESIDENTIAL weekly mean below +6.0 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS averaged -37.3 and RESIDENTIAL 6.3 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: When PARKS < -35.0 and RESIDENTIAL < +6.0 jointly, the following two-week RETAIL_REC mean is not above the preceding two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: In the partial-reopening regime where RETAIL_REC has held above -15 for three consecutive weeks, incremental policy relaxation passes straight through to retail activity, so the next week prints above the last four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC weekly mean stays above -15.0 for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC held between -13.4 and -14.6 for all four weekly means
regime_hint: partial reopening with retail floor above -15
failure_condition: The week following a three-week RETAIL_REC floor above -15.0 prints at or below the last-28-day mean of -14.0.

mechanism_narrative: Deeply negative PARKS values (-35 to -39) mark a seasonal cold regime that also suppresses discretionary retail trips; absent a PARKS rebound above -30, RETAIL_REC drifts lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stayed between -35.7 and -39.3 in every weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks exceeds the last-28-day mean of -14.0 while PARKS remains below -30.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT is the signature of a genuine reopening; when both improve in the same week while grocery stays flat, the effect compounds and lifts RETAIL_REC over four weeks by more than either series alone predicts.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve week-on-week while GROCERY_PHARM stays within 2 points of baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES -13.0 and TRANSIT -37.4 are the best of the four weekly means
failure_condition: The joint WORKPLACES-TRANSIT improvement does not produce a next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean above -14.0.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed flat within 2 points of baseline for four weeks, evidence that stockpiling behavior has ended; the released pantry budget shifts to discretionary retail, raising RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM four-week range stays within 2 points of 0.0
failure_condition: The week after a four-week GROCERY_PHARM range under 2 points, RETAIL_REC does not exceed the fourth week's reading of -13.4.
